displayName: Acme-ERP order/stock procedures (Java 21 + Spring Boot 3 + JUnit 5)
description: Reference OpenEdge ABL → Java-21 / Spring Boot 3 scaffold for the Acme-ERP order and stock procedures. Demonstrates the wide ABL→Java idiom gap end-to-end: a TEMP-TABLE working set becomes a record list (OrderLine); DEFINE SHARED session variables become an explicit injected SessionContextPort (never a static field); FIND/FOR EACH record phrases become repository ports that PRESERVE the lock mode (EXCLUSIVE-LOCK ⟶ @Lock(PESSIMISTIC_WRITE), NO-LOCK ⟶ read-only) and return Optional for the NOT-AVAILABLE guard; the block-scoped DO TRANSACTION becomes a single @Transactional per-batch boundary with real all-or-nothing rollback; NO-ERROR becomes explicit exception handling; and the Unknown value (?) is mapped to a nullable BigDecimal whose propagation + guard are reproduced. Builds OFFLINE through the maven-sidecar (pinned plugins + junit/assertj only, no Spring on the classpath) — the Spring/JPA constructs are documented @TargetMapping contracts, and the pure business logic (stock arithmetic, Unknown-value guard, batch atomicity) is real Java the JUnit suite verifies. There is NO source-execution equivalence gate for ABL (the Progress AVM is proprietary); the golden-dataset extraction score (18/18) plus this test suite are the verification, and that limitation is documented rather than stubbed.

matches.fallback: Used for openedge routines whose enclosing program is an order/stock procedure (temp-table, record-phrase, transaction-scoped, or shared-variable heavy).

verification.sourceExecutionEquivalenceReason: No free/OSS Progress OpenEdge runtime exists (the AVM is proprietary), so the ABL source cannot be executed to compare behaviour. This is documented, not stubbed.
